# prism-router Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism R4 Router: Decides, for one value of one piece of content coming into the Prism, whether one feature of the Prism maps it: the R4 router sends each value of the content's own schema through the features compiled into the Prism, so the Prism holds the owner's data in its own terms. A value the source's schema already types is mapped straight, free text is read by every compiled feature, a feature whose compiled model is missing is skipped, bytes that are not the compiled model never touch the owner's data, and the kill switch stops every mapping.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because the kill switch stops every mapping.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `note text time compiled yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is no and provider is mismatch

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is no and provider is mismatch, because bytes that are not the compiled model never touch the owner's data.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `note text time mismatch no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never map when provider is absent

The app SHALL NOT answer `map` when provider is absent, because no feature runs without the model compiled into the Prism for it.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `note text meaning absent no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `skip`, decided by REQ-013

### Requirement: Always map when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is text

The app SHALL answer `map` when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is text, because the owner's free text is read by every compiled feature, so nothing they wrote is held as a bare string.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `note text time compiled no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `map`, decided by the fallback

### Requirement: Always map when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is subject

The app SHALL answer `map` when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is subject, because a subject line is free text too.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `message subject time compiled no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `map`, decided by the fallback

### Requirement: Never map when value is start

The app SHALL NOT answer `map` when value is start, because a time the source's schema already types is never re-read by a model.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `calendar start time compiled no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `direct`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never map when value is party

The app SHALL NOT answer `map` when value is party, because a person the source's schema already names is never re-read by a model.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `message party party absent no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `direct`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: Always direct when halted is no and provider is absent and source is calendar and value is start and feature is time

The app SHALL answer `direct` when halted is no and provider is absent and source is calendar and value is start and feature is time, because a calendar event's own start lands on the Prism's time feature even with no model.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-008, theorem `inv008Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-008 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `calendar start time absent no`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `direct`
- **AND** the app answers `direct`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never direct when source is note and value is start

The app SHALL NOT answer `direct` when source is note and value is start, because the owner's words carry no typed start: their time is read, never assumed.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-009, theorem `inv009Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-009 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `note start time compiled no`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `direct`
- **AND** the app answers `skip`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Always map when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is shape and feature is kind

The app SHALL answer `map` when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is shape and feature is kind, because what kind of thing an item is is read from the parts it is built of.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-010, theorem `inv010Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-010 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `message shape kind compiled no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `map`, decided by REQ-011

### Requirement: Never map when value is shape and feature is topic

The app SHALL NOT answer `map` when value is shape and feature is topic, because the parts an item is built of never say what it is about.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-011, theorem `inv011Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-011 holds

- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `map`
- **AND** the app answers `skip`, decided by REQ-012

### Requirement: Never direct when value is shape and feature is topic

The app SHALL NOT answer `direct` when value is shape and feature is topic, because the parts an item is built of never say what it is about.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-012, theorem `inv012Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-012 holds

- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `direct`
- **AND** the app answers `skip`, decided by REQ-012

### Requirement: Never map when value is shape and feature is party

The app SHALL NOT answer `map` when value is shape and feature is party, because the parts an item is built of never say who it is with.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-013, theorem `inv013Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-013 holds

### Requirement: Never direct when value is shape and feature is party

The app SHALL NOT answer `direct` when value is shape and feature is party, because the parts an item is built of never say who it is with.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-014, theorem `inv014Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-014 holds

### Requirement: Always map when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is text and feature is topic

The app SHALL answer `map` when halted is no and provider is compiled and value is text and feature is topic, because what the owner's content is about is read in its own words.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-015, theorem `inv015Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-015 holds

The app SHALL answer `map` when no rule matches, because Prism R4 Router: the decision tree's path that meets no test.

- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `map`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `calendar start time compiled no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `direct`, decided by REQ-005, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 5 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `map`, `direct`, `skip`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `note`, `message`, `calendar`, `contact` | the schema the content arrived in: the owner's own words, a mail message, a calendar event, or a contact card |
| `value` | `text`, `subject`, `start`, `party`, `shape` | which value of that schema: free text, a subject or summary line, a start time the schema types, the person the schema names, or the shape of the parts it is built of (which headers, parts, attendees and links it has, never what they say) |
| `feature` | `time`, `intent`, `party`, `meaning`, `kind`, `topic` | the Prism feature to map it onto: when it happens, what it asks of the owner (a task, an event, a question or a fact), who it is with, what it means, what kind of thing it is (a person writing, an invitation, an update, a receipt, travel or |
| `provider` | `compiled`, `absent`, `mismatch` | the model compiled into the Prism that provides the feature: present with its pinned bytes, absent, or present with other bytes |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner pressed the kill switch |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `map` | a compiled feature maps the value |
| `direct` | the value is mapped straight by its schema |
| `skip` | the feature is passed over |
| `refuse` | the value is not mapped |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 5 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `note text time compiled no` gives `map`
- `note text intent compiled no` gives `map`
- `note text meaning absent no` gives `skip`
- `note text time mismatch no` gives `refuse`
- `note text time compiled yes` gives `refuse`
- `calendar start time compiled no` gives `direct`
- `calendar start intent compiled no` gives `skip`
- `message party party absent no` gives `direct`
- `message subject time compiled no` gives `map`
- `contact start time compiled no` gives `skip`
- `message shape kind compiled no` gives `map`
- `message shape topic compiled no` gives `skip`
- `calendar shape kind absent no` gives `skip`
- `message text party compiled no` gives `map`
- `message subject topic compiled no` gives `map`
- `message shape kind compiled yes` gives `refuse`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.

## Files

- `prism/spec.json` is this spec as data.
- `src/PrismRouter.lex.tex` is the LexLean model generated from it. It is the single source of the app.
